newsitem.title: GREECE: GOVERNMENT PLANS NEW TAXES TO FUND SOCIAL PROGRAMMES.
newsitem.headline: GOVERNMENT PLANS NEW TAXES TO FUND SOCIAL PROGRAMMES.

text.p: The government is planning the introduction of two new taxes targeting real estate and capital gains on share buyouts of non-listed companies, the Athens financial daily "Imerisia' reported on Wednesday.

Dubbed the 'solidarity tax', the tax on real estate will be used to finance government programmes for the unemployed and other recipients of social benefits through the proposed 'Cohesion and Solidarity Fund'.

Sources told Reuters National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou was urged by Development Minister Vasso Papandreou and Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis to come up with new taxes to fund government social programmes.
Papandoniou will reportedly work out the details and submit the proposal for the new taxes in the next two weeks.
According to Imerisia, the government is also seriously considering a capital gains tax of between 15-20 percent on share transfers of more than 51 percent, to be applied to non-listed companies.
Share transfers of listed companies and small and medium size enterprises will be exempted from the tax.
